Name: Qwen3.6 35B A3B
Notes: 128K context, q8 KV, flash attention, MTP draft head and 39 CPU expert layers. Matches scripts/qwen36-server.bat; workbench uses its own private port.

Name: Qwen3.6 Genesis / Hermes 35B A3B
Notes: 128K context, q8 KV, flash attention, MTP, all experts and vision projector on CPU, custom Genesis template. Matches scripts/qwen36-genesis-server.bat; workbench uses its own private port. Chat currently sends text only.

Name: Z-Image Turbo 6B (Apache 2.0)
PromptGuide: It reads the prompt with a Qwen3 language model, so it wants plain descriptive prose - full sentences, the way you would describe a photograph to someone - not comma-separated tags. It is a distilled 8-step model: it gets the main subject, setting and lighting right but paraphrases a long prompt and drops details that come late in it, so keep to 60-120 words with the things that matter first. It renders a few words of quoted text (a sign, a title) and not much more.
Notes: Fast. ~90 s at 1216x832 txt2img. Paraphrases long prompts. Commercial use OK. img2img, masked region edits and upscaling all work well; reference-image editing does not - use FLUX.2 klein for that.

Name: FLUX.2 klein 4B (Apache 2.0)
PromptGuide: It reads the prompt with a Qwen3 language model, so it wants plain descriptive prose - full sentences, subject first, then setting, lighting and style - not comma-separated tags. It is a distilled 4-step model run at guidance 1: there is no negative prompt, so say what should be in the picture rather than what should not, and keep to 40-100 words with the things that matter first. It renders a few words of quoted text. Given reference images it is an instruction editor instead: name what to change and what to keep ("Change the sign to read 'OPEN'; keep the street, the lighting and the framing identical").
Notes: Fastest: ~40 s at 1024x1024, half of Z-Image. The only installed model that edits from reference images (~85 s at 1024) - it needs no vision encoder for it. 4 steps at guidance 1, so the negative prompt does nothing. Commercial use OK.

Name: Qwen-Image 2.1 7B (research, non-commercial)
PromptGuide: It reads the prompt with a Qwen3-VL language model and follows a long prompt clause by clause, so be thorough: 100-250 words of plain descriptive prose covering subject, setting, composition, lighting and style. It is the best of the installed models at lettering: give the exact words in double quotes and describe the typeface, colour and where the text sits.
Notes: Slow (~7 min at 1216x832) but follows long prompts clause by clause. Best text rendering of the installed models. Good for region edits where the instruction is wordy.

Name: Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo 7B (research, non-commercial)
PromptGuide: It is a 6-step distillation of Qwen-Image 2.1 and reads the prompt the same way, with a Qwen3-VL language model that follows a long prompt clause by clause: 100-250 words of plain descriptive prose covering subject, setting, composition, lighting and style. It runs at guidance 1, so there is no negative prompt - describe what should be there. Lettering is good for signs and headlines: give the exact words in double quotes and describe the typeface, colour and where the text sits. Small, dense text is where it falls behind the full model, so keep rendered text short and large.
Notes: Qwen-Image 2.1 distilled to 6 steps by Viggle (v0.3), on the same encoder and VAE: under 2 min at 1024x1024, where the full model takes ~7 min at 1216x832. Always 6 steps at guidance 1 - the steps box and the negative prompt do nothing. Viggle rates it close to the full model on most prompts and behind it on small, dense text.

Name: FLUX.1 Kontext dev 12B (non-commercial)
PromptGuide: It is an instruction-editing model. Given an input or reference image, the prompt is a direct instruction naming what to change and what to keep ("Change the car to red; keep the street, the lighting and the framing identical"). With no image it works as text-to-image and wants 40-100 words of plain descriptive English. Either way the prompt goes through T5, which stops reading at about 500 tokens.
Notes: The instruction-edit model that actually works here: the flux_kontext preset feeds reference images straight from the VAE to the DiT, so it needs no vision encoder and sidesteps the Qwen3-VL problem entirely. On sd.cpp master, not an unmerged PR. Reuses the Flux VAE already installed for Z-Image. Run ./download-models.sh to fetch the rest (~10 GB). Slow on Pascal - budget several minutes per edit at 768.
